The broader attack surface appears to include multiple subdomains and infrastructure classes such as noVNC gateways, GitLab/assets hosts, reverse proxies, status/API services, and VM-related infrastructure, which are likely more productive targets than the heavily protected apex host.
findings.evidence: nuclei failed with: `[FTL] Could not run nuclei: could not create automatic scan service: could not get templates in directory: no templates found in path "/home/ngannguyen/nuclei-templates"`. Session context reports Vercel/edge protection and multiple intercepted paths: direct request to `https://tryhackme.com/api/` returned a `Vercel Security Checkpoint` HTML page; `https://tryhackme.com/_next/static/` returned an HTML page titled `Vercel Security Checkpoint`; `https://tryhackme.com/_next/data/` also returned a checkpoint page instead of Next.js data JSON. Katana only discovered the root URL and `/g`, suggesting crawl restriction by edge controls or JavaScript gating. Subfinder reportedly identified a broad attack surface including production VM infrastructure, reverse proxies, noVNC gateways, authentication setup, GitLab/assets hosts, status APIs, CDN/import-related hosts, and other subdomains.
